sources.title: Fijian War Club Inscriptions
sources.author: Fijian warriors
sources.excerpt: I am the club that breaks the waves, the tooth that bites the enemy.
sources.longExcerpt: I am the club that breaks the waves, the tooth that bites the enemy. This historical source from 1800 provides valuable insight into the oceania region during the industrial period. It represents the voices, experiences, and perspectives of people who lived during this transformative time in human history. Such primary sources are essential for understanding not just the major events of history, but the daily lives, beliefs, and struggles of ordinary people across different cultures and time periods.

sources.title: Typee
sources.author: Herman Melville
sources.excerpt: The Marquesas! What strange visions of outlandish things does the very name spirit up! Naked houris, cannibal banquets, groves of cocoa-nut, coral reefs, tattooed chiefs, and bamboo temples.
sources.longExcerpt: The Marquesas! What strange visions of outlandish things does the very name spirit up! Naked houris, cannibal banquets, groves of cocoa-nut, coral reefs, tattooed chiefs, and bamboo temples. This semi-autobiographical novel from 1846 by the future author of Moby-Dick shaped American perceptions of Polynesian culture, mixing genuine observation with romantic exoticism.

sources.title: In the South Seas
sources.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
sources.excerpt: The first experience can never be repeated. The first love, the first sunrise, the first South Sea island, are memories apart and touched a virginity of sense.
sources.longExcerpt: The first experience can never be repeated. The first love, the first sunrise, the first South Sea island, are memories apart and touched a virginity of sense. This travel narrative from 1896 by the author of Treasure Island provides detailed observations of Pacific island cultures during a period of rapid colonial change.
